decision: A pve-container build newer than the compatible-versions list is not untested on that ground alone: the overlay matches the checksum of the guarded files, each guard on its own, so judge a node from its journal line, never by version.

evidence.text: lib/PVE/LXC/BindSnap.pm keys the known-good table on the combined sha256 of @GUARDED_FILES. RED (opus) on the pre-edit text could not tell checksum from version; GREEN (opus, haiku) answered from the new text.

reopen_if: The overlay starts keying vetted builds on the package version.
why: Readers compared the node's version with the top of the list and concluded TEST mode, while an unchanged guarded file set validates as checksum-validated with no new row.

A rootfs-only snapshot misses every `mpN` volume

decision: On a build the guard refuses (snapshot gated / BLOCKED), offer a raw zfs snapshot of EVERY managed volume of a STOPPED CT whose managed volumes are all on zfspool storage, plus a copy of the CT config, before BINDSNAP-UNSUPPORTED; anything else (running CT, a managed volume on non-ZFS storage) goes to vzdump.

evidence.text: Refusal text and order checked in lib/PVE/LXC/BindSnap.pm (snapshot_create: known-BAD die, then the snapshot gated die). RED (opus) on the pre-edit text listed as gaps: rootfs-only, no rollback, no config copy, unsure the route applies to a bind-mount CT. GREEN (opus, haiku) on the new text snapshotted rootfs and mp0 together, saved the config, routed an lvmthin rootfs to vzdump, and quoted the pct rollback interaction. ZFS and Proxmox behaviour itself is documented, not run on a node.

reopen_if: The overlay's own refusal starts offering a safe route itself, or Proxmox's ZFS plugin stops refusing a rollback past a newer snapshot.
why: The gate message offers only updating pve-container or the at-your-own-risk marker, and the pre-edit skill named only a rootfs (disk-0) zfs snapshot from its Not-for paragraph, with no mpN volumes, no config copy, no rollback, and no word on how a raw snapshot interacts with pct rollback.

the node accepts only what its installed release holds
decision: The skill names no vetted pve-container range and no release that holds one: it points at docs/compatible-versions.md as the authoritative list for both guards, and says a node accepts only the rows its INSTALLED pve-bindsnap release holds, so update pve-bindsnap to pick up newer rows.

evidence.text: The pre-edit text named pve-bindsnap 1.4.1 and the range 6.0.18 to 6.1.16 while the repo was already at 1.4.2, which is the staleness the decision removes. Section 1 of the skill holds the apt-get upgrade and install.sh routes the new sentence points at. No RED/GREEN reader probe was run for this edit.

reopen_if: pve-bindsnap releases stop being automatic, or docs/compatible-versions.md stops being the list the release pipeline writes.
why: User decision 2026-11-18 "Skill stops naming a range": pve-bindsnap gets an hourly auto-vet and auto-release pipeline, so any range or release number written into the skill would go stale with the next automatic release while the compatible-versions page is regenerated with it.
